- `editor/core/verbs.py:663` `@command('map.tileset.grow', summary="Point a tileset at a re-cut sheet and change how many tiles it owns, without moving one placed gid. This is how a tileset stops being a fixed-size sheet: crop the region you want out of any image, write it under the old rows at the SAME WIDTH, and grow the count. Rows are the only safe axis -- a local tile id is row * columns + column and every reader takes that stride from the sheet's width, so a wider sheet renumbers every id after the first row and repaints the map with nothing raised.
